entries.name: Henry H. Franz

expected.charges: Refusing to wear the uniform or perform military service as a Mennonite Brethren conscientious objector during World War I.
expected.sentence:
Life imprisonment, reduced to 25 years; transferred to the Fort Leavenworth disciplinary barracks in June 1918, he died in custody there on December 1, 1918, at age 22.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — court-martialed at Camp Travis and sentenced to life imprisonment (one of 45 objectors), reduced to 25 years.

entries.rationale: Swarthmore curated WWI CO row explicitly states imprisoned June15,1918. Hooker Oklahoma Mennonite Brethren, Travis and Leavenworth, December1 death all match. Source Henry E variant is already explained in profile. Local three-swarthmore-Franz.json preserves row.
